title: Late V1 dispatcher registration bricks migrate() for affected holders via index-0 mintFor revert
description: setInitialized() (NFTMigrator.sol:51-58) validates indexMapping only for indexes 1..v1.nextIndex()-1 at the time it is called and is one-way. If the independently-owned V1 NFTMinter owner later registers a new dispatcher (NFTMinter.sol:127-128 increments v1.nextIndex()), the migrator's indexMapping[newIndex] remains 0. A holder of newIndex calling migrate() burns the V1 NFTs (line 68) then calls v2.mintFor(0, msg.sender) (lines 69-71) because indexMapping[newIndex]==0; mintFor reverts at 'NFTMinterV2: index not registered' (NFTMinterV2.sol:208) since configs[0].dispatcher==address(0) (V2 nextIndex starts at 1). The whole tx reverts, rolling back the burn but leaving migration bricked for that index.
impact: No direct asset loss. Migration becomes unavailable for holders of any V1 index registered after the migrator was initialized. V1 NFTs retain their utility. State is recoverable by a migrator-owner action (setMapping for the missing index). Holders of other indexes are unaffected (balance==0 at newIndex skips the iteration).
attackPath: 1. Migrator owner configures mappings for all current V1 indexes and calls setInitialized() (NFTMigrator.sol:51-58), which validates indexMapping only for indexes 1..v1.nextIndex()-1 AT THAT TIME and is one-way.
2. Later, the V1 NFTMinter owner (a distinct trust principal from the migrator owner) registers a new dispatcher, incrementing v1.nextIndex() (NFTMinter.sol:127-128).
3. The migrator's indexMapping[newIndex] is still 0 (never set; setInitialized cannot be re-run meaningfully and did not cover newIndex).
4. A holder of newIndex calls migrate(); the loop reaches i=newIndex, burns the V1 NFTs (NFTMigrator.sol:68), then calls v2.mintFor(0, msg.sender) because indexMapping[newIndex]==0 (lines 69-71).
5. mintFor reverts at 'NFTMinterV2: index not registered' (NFTMinterV2.sol:208) since configs[0].dispatcher==address(0) (V2 nextIndex starts at 1).
6. The entire migrate() tx reverts (the burn is rolled back), so the holder of newIndex cannot migrate until the mapping is fixed. Holders of other indexes are unaffected.
likelihood: medium - requires post-initialization V1 dispatcher registration by the V1 owner; cross-contract ordering coupling, not a single-owner reckless mistake.
assumptions: V1 owner registers a new dispatcher after the migrator is initialized, and at least one user holds that new index.
externalRequirements: Action by the independently-owned V1 NFTMinter contract owner after migrator initialization.
recommendation: Either skip (rather than burn-then-revert on) indexes whose indexMapping is unset so migrate() degrades gracefully, validate indexMapping[i] != 0 before burning each index, or allow the migrator owner to extend mappings post-initialization for indexes registered after setInitialized(). Document the required ordering coupling between the two owners.
justification: Availability of the migration flow is impacted for a subset of holders due to cross-contract ordering coupling between two independently-owned contracts (not pure single-owner self-harm, so KI-1/KI-4 do not fully absorb it). No assets are stolen or permanently lost: V1 NFTs remain usable and the migrator owner can restore migration via setMapping. Recoverability and partial scope keep this firmly at Medium, not High.
borderlineFlag: BORDERLINE for severity-auditor: recoverable by the migrator owner adding the missing mapping, and the trigger is a privileged V1-owner action. If the auditor treats the cross-contract coupling as fully owner-trust-covered, this could drop to Low/QA. Kept at Medium because the two owners are distinct trust principals and migrate() silently bricks (burns-then-reverts) rather than degrading gracefully.
